Tasks: 113 DeepSWE tasks (pinned commits, shallow clone at base commit). Configurations: 16 models with fixed reasoning effort (explicit for some families, provider default for others). Baseline: none designated; cross-benchmark comparison with publicly reported SWE-Bench Pro scores, and a matched audit on 30 SWE-Bench Pro tasks run through the same pipeline. Held constant: harness (mini-swe-agent commit adfe2023, single bash tool, shared prompt), 9,000 s timeout, no step or cost cap. Acceptance tests: hand-written functional verifiers plus regression checks, each verifier run three times during authoring to remove flakiness. Repetitions: ~4 rollouts per task (pass@1 and pass@4, run-to-run CI). Human intervention: none. Runs collected May 2026

GPT-5.5 clearly top (70.0%, CI apart from others); GPT-5.4 (55.5%) and Opus 4.7 (54.2%) overlap and are not statistically separated; Haiku 4.5 and MiniMax-M2.7 at 0.2%. DeepSWE spreads eight models over 69.8 points vs 29.7 on SWE-Bench Pro. Output tokens, wall-clock time and cost per trial vary by an order of magnitude but none correlates strongly with pass rate. Verifier disagreement with the LLM judge: 1.4% (10/735) for DeepSWE vs 32.4% (256/789) for SWE-Bench Pro (Clopper-Pearson CIs [0.7, 2.5] and [29.2, 35.8]). Claude configurations miss enumerated requirements most often; Opus configurations recover the gold fix from .git history on SWE-Bench Pro (~13% of trials; 18% of Opus 4.7 and 25% of Opus 4.6 passes judged improper); Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.4 write new tests in >80% of DeepSWE runs. Harness pilot differences not significant

It separated frontier models over a wider band than SWE-Bench Pro, though mid-table configurations overlap. Repeatability: ~4 runs per configuration; authors note the run-to-run CI ignores task-sampling variance and is unreliable with four runs (Wilson interval for GPT-5.5 wider: [65.6, 74.1]). Limitations stated: binary reward without partial credit; functional correctness only; prompts more specified than real requests; under-specified and interactive use not measured; single harness and mixed reasoning-effort settings; small audit with single-digit DeepSWE counts and a GPT-5.5 judge that may favour its own family; harness pilot only n = 10; wider spread is not itself a capability claim

Limitations: binary pass/fail; no code-quality scoring; middle-band prompt specification; ambiguous requests, non-coding uses and interactive collaboration unmeasured; fixed harness bypasses native editing primitives; reasoning-effort mix; verifier audit small and judge fallible; pilot not a ranking of production harnesses; 'long-horizon' is a structural property, not human time; decontamination holds only at evaluation time. Future work: run models under multiple harnesses; broader repositories and more bug localization and refactoring tasks; add C++ and Java; black-box and hybrid LLM-judge/unit-test verifiers
